questions.prompt: The Big Dig was the most expensive highway project in U.S. history. What was the approximate final cost?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Almost fifteen billion dollars. Originally budgeted at two billion. Cost overruns, corruption, mistakes. But it worked. Mostly.
questions.npcReactionWrong: The Big Dig changed everything. Twenty years of construction. Almost fifteen billion dollars. Think about that number.

questions.prompt: What highway did the Big Dig bury underground, and what greenspace was built above it?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: The Central Artery. Now it's the Rose Kennedy Greenway. The highway used to divide the city. Now the park connects it.
questions.npcReactionWrong: They buried the Central Artery. Interstate 93. Put the Rose Kennedy Greenway on top. Named after JFK's mother.

questions.prompt: The Seaport District was previously known by what description due to its industrial past?
choices: South Boston Waterfront / industrial warehouses and fishing
questions.npcReactionCorrect: It was warehouses, fishing, industrial. South Boston Waterfront. Nobody wanted to live here. Now look at it. Sully barely recognized it at the end.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Before the condos and restaurants, this was all warehouses and fishing. Industrial waterfront. Completely transformed.

questions.prompt: What museum in the Seaport houses historic ships where you can reenact a famous protest?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: The Tea Party Ships museum. They have replica ships. You can throw the tea. Every tourist does it. Sully did it three times.
questions.npcReactionWrong: The Boston Tea Party Ships museum. You can reenact throwing tea overboard. Tourist trap, but a fun one.

questions.prompt: What tunnel connects the Seaport to Logan Airport, and approximately how long is it?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Ted Williams Tunnel. About a mile and a half. Part of the Big Dig. Sully used to drive through it just to feel like he was underwater.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Ted Williams Tunnel. Named after the baseball legend. About 1.6 miles. Opened in 1995.

alternateQuestions.prompt: The Institute of Contemporary Art moved to the Seaport in what year, helping spark development?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: 2006. One building changed everything here. The ICA was the catalyst.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: 2006. When the ICA moved to the waterfront, everything started to change.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What convention center anchors the Seaport District?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Boston Convention and Exhibition Center. BCEC. Biggest in New England. Brought a lot of suits to this neighborhood.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: The BCEC. Boston Convention and Exhibition Center. Massive. Brings people from everywhere.

alternateQuestions.prompt: The Seaport has been criticized for lacking what, compared to other Boston neighborhoods?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Affordability. Diversity. The Seaport is beautiful but expensive. Not everyone can afford to live here. That's the tradeoff.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Critics say it's too expensive, too exclusive. The Seaport looks beautiful but it's missing the soul of old Boston.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What major technology and pharmaceutical companies have headquarters or major offices in the Seaport?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Vertex, Amazon regional offices, a dozen others. The Seaport isn't just condos. It's become Boston's innovation district.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Big pharma, big tech. Vertex Pharmaceuticals has their headquarters here. Amazon has a big presence. Money follows money.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What body of water does the Seaport District border?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Boston Harbor. Fort Point Channel on one side. Basic geography, but you'd be surprised how many people don't know.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Boston Harbor. The Seaport is on the waterfront. That's the whole point. Water defines this neighborhood.
